To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the differences in diabetes prevalence between the Pima Indian and South Asian populations are not related to differences in the insulin secretion or insulin metabolism, but rather to differences in insulin action.

Pima Indians have higher fasting insulin concentrations than do South Asians and whites, even after adjusting for obesity; Pima Indians have a lower proportion of proinsulins than do South Asians or whites; and the risk of diabetes is not related to insulin secretion.

Pima Indians are hyperinsulinemic compared with South Asians and whites, even when specific assays are used, and that the hyperinsulinemia in Pima Indians is due to enhanced insulin production, whereas in subjects with type 2 DM, hyperinsulinemia may be related to insulin resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes.
the study of the etiopathogenesis of type 2 diabetes mellitus in Pima Indians.
the study of insulin resistance, insulin secretion, β-cell function, and insulin metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of diabetes is not due to insulin resistance alone but is due to a combination of insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia and defective β-cell function.
the risk of diabetes is related to obesity, insulin resistance, and β-cell failure.
the differences in risk of type 2 diabetes between these three groups are due to differences in obesity, insulin sensitivity, and possibly in the rate of β-cell loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pima Indians, Asians, and whites have different degrees of insulin resistance and that the risk of diabetes is related to the severity of insulin resistance.
the risk of diabetes is not due to differences among populations in insulin secretion or processing.
the Pima Indians have an increased risk of type 2 diabetes because of insulin resistance and impaired insulin action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hyperinsulinemia in type 2 diabetes is not simply due to insulin resistance.
the differences in insulin secretion and insulin processing among the three ethnic groups are not the cause of the differences in risk of diabetes.
insulin assays that measure intact insulin are more sensitive to changes in insulin secretion than are assays that measure total insulin.
